data.title: Maine's Comprehensive Privacy Bill (LD 1822) Fails on Final House Vote

sources.title: Maine rejects comprehensive data privacy law, again
sources.key_facts: Second House vote rejecting LD 1822; session ends April 15; business pushback.

sources.title: Maine Senate votes to keep controversial data privacy bill alive
sources.key_facts: Senate 18-14 vote on April 6, 2026 to send LD 1822 back to House.

sources.title: Data privacy déjà vu as bill bounces between chambers
sources.key_facts: Political-org exemption dispute caused ping-pong between chambers.

sources.title: New political group exemption narrows support
sources.key_facts: Exemption for political organizations was late-added and controversial.

sources.title: Fear of the unknown toll on businesses likely to sink data privacy bill
sources.key_facts: Business groups lobbied against bill; House Democrats flipping.

sources.title: LD 1822, HP 1220 — Text and Status (Maine Legislature)
sources.key_facts: Official bill page: sponsor Rep. Amy Kuhn, 132nd Legislature, Maine Online Data Privacy Act.

sources.title: House approves Kuhn bill to strengthen Maine's data privacy laws
sources.key_facts: Substantive provisions: data minimization, consumer rights, minor protections, biometric limits, July 1 2026 effective date.

sources.title: Proposed State Privacy Law Update: April 6, 2026
sources.key_facts: Confirms LD 1822 stalling on procedural House vote; April 15 session deadline.

sources.title: EPIC Testimony in Support of LD 1822
Maine House Passes Landmark Privacy Bill — ACLU of Maine
sources.key_facts: Corroborates initial House passage and substantive scope of LD 1822.
